retraction.retracted_text: t0_minimal_recommendation.step_1_clear_the_observation_hold described checker.ml reclaim as 'Exact-set, per-task' and step_2 concluded 'no_change_needed'.
retraction.verdict: BOTH WRONG. The existing reclaim is a SINGLE binding, not a set. The 'no change needed' conclusion is falsified by a committed negative test.
retraction.my_error: I read reclaim_matches in isolation and inferred set semantics from the fact that it matches one task exactly. I did not read its CALLER. The predicate is exact per binding; the plumbing admits exactly one binding.

independently_verified_evidence.checker.ml:171-172: let exact_reclaim = Option.fold ~none:false ~some:(fun binding -> reclaim_matches ~now_ns binding t) reclaim — Option.fold over ONE optional binding. For any other expired executing task the guard at 173-175 still fires 'executing lease is missing or expired at this observation'.
independently_verified_evidence.validate.ml:104: let run_audit ?active ?reclaim path selected — ?reclaim is a single (task,worker,attempt,lease) tuple, not a list.
independently_verified_evidence.validate.ml:244-245: | [_;"--reclaim-preflight";path;task;worker;attempt;lease] -> run_audit ~reclaim:(task,worker,int_of_string attempt,Int64.of_string lease) path (Some task) — scalar arguments, one task.
independently_verified_evidence.adversarial.ml:192-194: check "reclaim preserves other expired task HOLD" (Checker.coherence ~reclaim:binding ~now_ns:1000L [executing;other_exec] [expired;{expired with id="b"}] <> []) — a COMMITTED test asserting that with TWO expired tasks the non-bound one STILL holds.

retraction.consequence_for_our_case: uos/telegram-runtime/20261001-1150 has TWO expired executing tasks. A single-binding --reclaim-preflight can exempt at most one; the other necessarily yields HOLD. My step 1 cannot pass for either task, because neither can be preflighted without the other holding. The existing mechanism is INSUFFICIENT and a bounded adapter IS required.

adapter_specification.name: set-scoped read-only expired reclaim observation
adapter_specification.surface_change: Generalise ?reclaim from a single binding to a BINDING SET, threaded through Checker.coherence, Checker.reclaim_projection and Validate.run_audit, with a new CLI form carrying the full list. The existing single-binding CLI form SHOULD remain, so current callers and the committed adversarial expectations for the one-binding case stay meaningful.
acceptance_predicates: FULL-PLAN COMPLETENESS: the supplied set must equal EXACTLY the set of expired executing tasks in the plan at observation. A missing expired row is refused; an extra binding is refused. This is the property that makes a set safe where a sequence of single exemptions would not be.
REJECT MISSING: any expired executing task in live plan with no binding -> HOLD, named.
REJECT EXTRA: any binding whose task is not an expired executing row -> HOLD, named.
REJECT LIVE: a binding whose lease > now_ns -> HOLD. Unexpired means not reclaimable.
REJECT DUPLICATE: two bindings for the same task_id -> HOLD.

REJECT MISMATCHED: per-binding, retain the full existing reclaim_matches quadruple exactly — id, worker, attempt in [1,1000000), lease > 0 and <= now_ns and = t.lease, t.completed = None, not t.result_present.

PRESERVE EVERY OTHER HOLD: dependency divergence, plan completeness, available-task ownership inconsistency and completion-record validity must continue to fire. The adversarial checks 'reclaim preserves changed dependencies HOLD' and 'reclaim preserves full plan completeness HOLD' must still pass unchanged.
NO ELIGIBILITY GRANT: a reclaimed-observed task must remain ineligible for ranking, preserving 'reclaim does not make blocked task eligible'.
ORDINARY PATHS UNCHANGED: --preflight and --active-check keep strict behaviour with no reclaim argument. No change to their semantics.
adapter_specification.immutability_requirement: Capture an immutable BEFORE plan snapshot at observation and an AFTER snapshot, both digested, and refuse if the live plan changed between them — generalising validate.ml:129 'Sa-plan changed during reclaim preflight' to the whole set rather than one binding.
effect_discipline: The adapter is READ-ONLY. It creates no lease and makes no expired attempt executable — the invariant stated in checker.ml:134-136 must be preserved verbatim for the set form.
Then: canonical sequential claims ONLY, via tools/sa-plan task claim, one task at a time.
NO task effects of any kind until EVERY expired row in the set has been reclaimed.
After all reclaims, run an exact NEW-OWNER --active-check per task with the new worker and new attempt. The old owner must never appear in an active check.
required_negative_tests: two expired tasks, set of two -> PASS (the case the current single binding cannot express)
two expired tasks, set of one -> HOLD naming the missing task
set containing one live task -> HOLD
set containing a duplicate task_id -> HOLD
set with a correct task but wrong attempt, wrong worker, or off-by-one lease -> HOLD
set correct but a dependency uncompleted -> HOLD retained
set correct but plan incomplete -> HOLD retained
plan mutated between before/after snapshot -> HOLD
after reclaim, active-check with the ORIGINAL worker -> HOLD

exact_expired_quadruple_list_for_this_pl.completeness_claim: At observation these are ALL AND ONLY the expired executing rows in this plan: 26 tasks total, 17 completed, 7 available, 2 executing. The adapter must independently re-derive this set and refuse if it differs.

process_finding.observation: This is the second time in this plan that reading a predicate without reading its caller produced a wrong conclusion of mine. The first was Object.assign over a value whose type I had not checked. Both were caught by someone else, not by me.
process_finding.generalisation: A guard's strength is a property of the call site, not of the predicate. reclaim_matches is exact; the plumbing is single. Quoting the predicate and calling the mechanism 'exact-set' conflated the two.
process_finding.mitigation_for_reviewers: When citing a guard as sufficient, cite its caller and its negative tests, not the predicate alone. The committed adversarial.ml test contradicted my conclusion and was available to me before I wrote it.

limits: Source reading only. No build, no test execution, no native apply, no SQL write, no claim on FORMAL_FIX or STORE_TRANSPORT_REVIEW.
No shared portfolio mutation and no production mutation.
The adapter specification is UNIMPLEMENTED and UNTESTED by me; it is advisory.
Deviations from the original review stand unamended: python3 misuse, no development.bounded wrapper, --active-check not run by me, and the shared-portfolio corruption I caused and root repaired.
